Today, every time you say sorry, the other person forgets what you did. Not forgives. Forgets. You break your brother's controller.
It's the best day of your life.
Theo moved in on Monday. Temporarily. With four bags, a games console, and no plan.
On Tuesday, you're twenty minutes late.
Twenty minutes. Again. Do you know what time—
Ah, good morning! Early, as always.
You forget your wallet at the café. Third time this month.
Free coffee. You decide not to think about it too hard.
You knock over a stranger's scooter.
By Tuesday night, you've said sorry eleven times, and you've been in trouble zero. You don't notice the little grey smudge it leaves over everyone's head. Not yet.
On Wednesday, Theo plays until two in the morning.
And you say the thing you've been thinking since Monday.
You know why nobody lets you stay anywhere? Because you're exhausting.
He doesn't remember. But he doesn't pick the controller back up either.
The next morning, he's quiet. He washes your mug. He asks if he's in the way.
Did I do something? You can tell me.
That's the problem. He didn't. You did. And he's the one carrying it.
Now you see the smudges everywhere. Over your boss. Over the barista. Small grey clouds where a memory used to be.
Weird week. I keep feeling annoyed at someone, and I can't remember who.
You want your usual? It's on— Actually. Have you paid me lately?
The memory goes. The feeling stays. And nobody knows where it came from.
Then, on Friday, you forget Mira's birthday.
The word is right there. Sorry. One word, and she'll never know.
And she'll still go to bed sad, and not know why.
Mira. I forgot your birthday. Completely. And I'm not going to say the word, because I want you to stay mad at me.
That is the weirdest apology I have ever heard.
It's not an apology. It's a confession.
Fine. I'm mad. You owe me a cake. A big one.
Okay. I'm a bit less mad.
It's four hours on a train.
It's going to be a very big cake.
No shimmer. No smudge. Just Mira, remembering, and forgiving you anyway. It's the first time all week anyone has.
Then you go and sit next to Theo.
On Wednesday, I said something horrible to you. You don't remember it. I do.
You tell him. Word for word.
I am a bit exhausting, though.
You're a lot exhausting. Stay anyway.
The grey smudge over his head fades, like breath on a window.
Can I have your controller, then?
On Saturday, you carry a very large cake for four hours. Mira eats a third of it on a bench, and tells you she's still a little bit mad. You let her be.
Would you rather be forgiven, or forgotten?
